translations.literal: At length he rode alone to distant outskirts and slept alone in deep wilds; he personally wielded spears and halberds and himself performed dismemberment; white blades were his playthings and killing his constant occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He rode alone to distant outskirts and slept alone in deep wilds; he personally wielded spears and halberds and himself performed dismemberment; naked blades were his playthings and killing his constant task.

sentences.zh: 捨交戟之衞，委天畢之儀，趨步闤闠，酣歌壚肆，宵遊忘反，宴寢營舍，奪人子女，掠人財物，方筴所不書，振古所未聞。

translations.literal: He abandoned the guard of crossed halberds and cast off celestial canopy ceremony; he ran through marketplaces and drank and sang in taverns; night outings forgot return, and feasting and sleeping were in barracks; he seized people's sons and daughters and plundered people's goods—what the records do not record, unheard since antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: He abandoned halberd guards and cast off canopy ceremony; he ran through marketplaces and drank and sang in taverns; night outings knew no return; he feasted and slept in barracks; he seized people's children and plundered their goods—unrecorded in the annals, unheard since antiquity.

sentences.zh: 沈勃儒士，孫超功臣，幼文兄弟，並豫勳効，四人無罪，一朝同戮。

translations.literal: Shen Bo was a Confucian scholar; Sun Chao was a meritorious minister; the You-wen brothers had shared in achievements—all four innocent, yet in one morning they were jointly executed.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Bo was a Confucian scholar; Sun Chao was a meritorious minister; the Youwen brothers had shared in meritorious service—all four innocent, yet in one morning they were executed together.

sentences.zh: 飛鏃鼓劍，孩稚無遺，屠裂肝腸，以為戲謔，投骸江流，以為歡笑。

translations.literal: He loosed flying bolts and beat swords; no child was spared; he butchered and split liver and guts as jest and cast corpses into the river as merriment.
translations.idiomatic: He loosed flying bolts and beat his sword; no child was spared; he butchered and split bodies for sport and cast corpses into the river for amusement.

sentences.zh: 又淫費無度，帑藏空竭，橫賦關河，專充別蓄，黔庶嗷嗷，厝生無所。

translations.literal: Moreover he squandered without limit; treasuries stood empty; he levied across the passes and rivers to fill private stores; the common folk wailed bitterly, with no place to set their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he squandered without limit until the treasuries stood empty; he levied across the passes and rivers to fill private stores; the common folk wailed bitterly with nowhere to live.

sentences.zh: 吾與其所生每厲以義方，遂謀酖毒，將騁凶忿。

translations.literal: I and his birth-mother repeatedly admonished him with righteous discipline, whereupon he plotted poison and was about to unleash vicious rage.
translations.idiomatic: I and his birth-mother repeatedly admonished him with righteous discipline; he then plotted poison and was about to unleash vicious fury.

sentences.zh: 沈憂假日，慮不終朝。

translations.literal: Deep grief consumed days; I feared not to survive the morning.
translations.idiomatic: Deep grief consumed my days; I feared I might not survive the morning.

sentences.zh: 自昔辛、癸，爰及幽、厲，方之於此，未譬萬分。

translations.literal: From old Xin and Gui down to You and Li—compared with this, not one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: From Xin and Gui of old down to You and Li—compared with this, not one part in ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 民怨既深，神怒已積，七廟阽危，四海褫氣。

translations.literal: Popular resentment had grown deep, divine wrath had accumulated; the seven ancestral temples tottered on the brink, and the four seas lost their breath.
translations.idiomatic: Popular resentment ran deep, divine wrath had accumulated; the seven ancestral temples tottered on the brink and the four seas held their breath in dread.

sentences.zh: 廢昏立明，前代令範，況迺滅義反道，天人所棄，釁深牧野，理絕桐宮。

translations.literal: Deposing the benighted and installing the enlightened is a fine model of former ages—how much more when one extinguishes righteousness and opposes the Way, abandoned by Heaven and man, guilt deeper than Muye, reason severed as at Tong Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Deposing the benighted and installing the enlightened is a fine model of former ages—how much more when one extinguishes righteousness and opposes the Way, abandoned by Heaven and man, with guilt deeper than at Muye and justification as clear as the confinement at Tong Palace.

sentences.zh: 故密令蕭領軍潛運明略，幽顯協規，普天同泰。

translations.literal: Therefore I secretly ordered Commander Xiao to deploy a bright design in secret; the hidden and manifest joined in plan, and all Heaven shared peace.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I secretly ordered Commander Xiao to deploy his design in secret; the visible and invisible realms joined in counsel, and all under Heaven would share peace.

sentences.zh: 驃騎大將軍安成王體自太宗，天挺淹叡，風神凝遠，德映在田。

translations.literal: Grand General of Rapid Cavalry Prince of Ancheng derives his person from Taizong; Heaven endowed him with profound wisdom; his spirit and bearing are composed and far-reaching; his virtue shines in field and farm.
translations.idiomatic: Grand general of rapid cavalry Prince of Ancheng descends from Taizong; Heaven endowed him with profound wisdom; his bearing is composed and far-reaching; his virtue shines even in retirement.

sentences.zh: 地隆親茂，皇曆攸歸，億兆係心，含生屬望。

translations.literal: His station is lofty and kinship flourishing; the imperial succession is his to receive; the hundred millions bind their hearts to him, and all living beings turn their hopes to him.
translations.idiomatic: His station is lofty and kinship flourishing; the imperial succession is rightly his; the hundred millions bind their hearts to him, and all living beings turn their hopes to him.

sentences.zh: 宜光奉祖宗，臨享萬國。

translations.literal: It is fitting that he brightly serve the ancestors and preside over and receive tribute from the myriad states.
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting that he brightly serve the ancestors and preside over the myriad states.

sentences.zh: 便依舊典，以時奉行。

translations.literal: Let the former canon be followed and timely observed.
translations.idiomatic: Let the former canon be followed and enacted in due season.

sentences.zh: 未亡人追往傷懷，永言感絕。

translations.literal: This survivor, recalling the past, is wounded in heart; long do I speak of grief beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: This survivor, looking back on the past, is wounded in heart; my grief passes words.

sentences.zh: 太后又令曰：「昱窮凶極暴，自取灰滅，雖曰罪招，能無傷悼。

translations.literal: The empress dowager again issued an order: "Yu was utterly vicious and extremely brutal and brought extinction upon himself; though his guilt invited it, can one not mourn?
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager again issued an order: "Yu was utterly vicious and extremely brutal and brought ruin upon himself; though crime summoned it, can one not mourn?

sentences.zh: 棄同品庶，顧所不忍。

translations.literal: To discard him as commoners are discarded is what I cannot bear to see.
translations.idiomatic: To treat him as commoners are discarded is what I cannot bear.

sentences.zh: 可特追封蒼梧郡王。

translations.literal: Let him be specially posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Cangwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Let him be specially posthumously enfeoffed as prince of Cangwu commandery.

sentences.zh: 」葬丹陽秣陵縣郊壇西。

translations.literal: " He was buried west of the suburban altar in Moling county, Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: " He was buried west of the suburban altar at Moling in Danyang.

sentences.zh: 初昱在東宮，年五六歲時，始就書學，而惰業好嬉戲，主帥不能禁。

translations.literal: Early on, when Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six years of age he first entered book learning, yet was lazy in his studies and fond of play; the commandant could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, when Yu was in the Eastern Palace, at five or six he first began formal study, yet was lazy and fond of play; the instructor could not restrain him.

sentences.zh: 好緣漆帳竿，去地丈餘，如此者半食久，乃下。

translations.literal: He loved to climb lacquered curtain poles more than a zhang above ground; thus for half a meal's time before coming down.
translations.idiomatic: He loved to climb lacquered curtain poles more than a zhang above the ground, staying there for half a mealtime before coming down.

sentences.zh: 年漸長，喜怒乖節，左右有失旨者，輒手加撲打。

translations.literal: As he gradually grew, joy and anger violated proper measure; attendants who missed his intent were immediately beaten with his hand.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew, joy and anger lost proper measure; attendants who displeased him were immediately beaten.

sentences.zh: 徒跣蹲踞，以此為常。

translations.literal: Barefoot and squatting—this became his custom.
translations.idiomatic: Going barefoot and squatting became his habit.

sentences.zh: 主帥以白太宗，上輒敕昱所生，嚴加捶訓。

translations.literal: The commandant reported to Taizong, and the emperor repeatedly ordered Yu's birth-mother to beat and instruct him severely.
translations.idiomatic: The instructor reported to Taizong, and the emperor repeatedly ordered Yu's birth-mother to beat and instruct him severely.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，內畏太后，外憚諸大臣，猶未得肆志。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, inwardly he feared the empress dowager and outwardly dreaded the chief ministers; he still could not fully indulge his will.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded to the throne, he still feared the empress dowager within and dreaded the chief ministers without; he could not yet fully indulge his will.

sentences.zh: 自加元服，變態轉興，內外稍無以制。

translations.literal: From the time of his capping, transformations and excesses arose, and inside and outside gradually none could restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: From the time he came of age, his excesses multiplied, and gradually none inside or outside the palace could restrain him.

sentences.zh: 三年秋冬間，便好出遊行，太妃每乘青篾車，隨相檢攝。

translations.literal: Between autumn and winter of the third year he took to going out to roam; the grand imperial consort each time rode in a green bamboo carriage to follow and keep watch.
translations.idiomatic: Between autumn and winter of the third year he took to roaming abroad; the grand imperial consort each time rode in a green bamboo carriage to follow and restrain him.

sentences.zh: 昱漸自放恣，太妃不復能禁。

translations.literal: Yu gradually indulged himself without restraint; the grand imperial consort could no longer restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Yu gradually indulged himself without restraint; the grand imperial consort could no longer check him.

sentences.zh: 單將左右，棄部伍，或十里、二十里，或入市里，或往營署，日暮乃歸。

translations.literal: Alone he led attendants, abandoning ranks—sometimes ten or twenty li, sometimes entering market neighborhoods, sometimes going to barracks and offices, returning only at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: Alone he led attendants, abandoning his escort—sometimes ten or twenty li, sometimes entering market neighborhoods, sometimes visiting barracks and offices, returning only at dusk.

sentences.zh: 四年春夏，此行彌數。

translations.literal: In spring and summer of the fourth year such outings grew ever more frequent.
translations.idiomatic: In spring and summer of the fourth year these outings became ever more frequent.

sentences.zh: 自京城剋定，意志轉驕，於是無日不出。

translations.literal: Since the capital rebellion was pacified, his will turned ever more arrogant, and from then on not a day passed without his going out.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital rebellion was pacified, his arrogance grew, and from then on he went out every day without fail.

sentences.zh: 與左右人解僧智、張五兒恒相馳逐，夜出，開承明門，夕去晨反，晨出暮歸。

translations.literal: With attendants Jie Seng-zhi and Zhang Wu-er he constantly raced in pursuit; going out at night, opening Chenming Gate, leaving at dusk and returning at dawn, or leaving at dawn and returning at dusk.
translations.idiomatic: With attendants Jie Sengzhi and Zhang Wu'er he constantly raced in pursuit; going out at night through Chenming Gate, he would leave at dusk and return at dawn, or leave at dawn and return at dusk.

sentences.zh: 從者並執鋋矛，行人男女，及犬馬牛驢，值無免者。

translations.literal: Followers all bore halberds and spears; men and women on the road, and dogs, horses, oxen, and donkeys—none encountered escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: Followers all bore halberds and spears; men and women on the road, and dogs, horses, oxen, and donkeys—none who met them escaped harm.

sentences.zh: 民間擾懼，晝日不敢開門，道上行人殆絕。

translations.literal: The common folk were disturbed and afraid; by day they dared not open doors, and travelers on the roads nearly vanished.
translations.idiomatic: The common folk were terrified; by day they dared not open their doors, and travelers on the roads nearly disappeared.

sentences.zh: 常著小袴褶，未嘗服衣冠。

translations.literal: He constantly wore short trousers and jackets and never wore cap and gown.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly wore short trousers and jackets and never wore formal cap and gown.

sentences.zh: 或有忤意，輒加以虐刑。

translations.literal: If anyone displeased him, he immediately inflicted cruel punishments.
translations.idiomatic: If anyone displeased him, he immediately inflicted cruel punishment.

sentences.zh: 有白棓數十枚，各有名號，鍼椎鑿鋸之徒，不離左右。

translations.literal: He had dozens of white clubs, each with a name; awls, mallets, chisels, and saws never left his side.
translations.idiomatic: He kept dozens of white clubs, each with its own name; awls, mallets, chisels, and saws were always at hand.

sentences.zh: 嘗以鐵椎椎人陰破，左右人見之有斂眉者，昱大怒，令此人袒胛正立，以矛刺胛洞過。

translations.literal: Once he crushed a man's groin with an iron mallet until it burst; when attendants who saw it knit their brows, Yu flew into rage and ordered that man to bare his shoulder and stand upright, then had a spear thrust through the shoulder, piercing through.
translations.idiomatic: Once he crushed a man's groin with an iron mallet; when attendants who saw it knit their brows, Yu flew into rage and ordered that man to bare his shoulder and stand upright, then had a spear thrust through it, piercing clear through.

sentences.zh: 於耀靈殿上養驢數十頭，所自乘馬，養於御牀側。

translations.literal: In the Hall of Dazzling Spirit he kept dozens of donkeys; the horse he himself rode was kept beside the imperial couch.
translations.idiomatic: In the Hall of Dazzling Spirit he kept dozens of donkeys; the horse he rode was kept beside the imperial couch.

sentences.zh: 先是民間訛言，謂太宗不男，陳太妃本李道兒妾，道路之言，或云道兒子也。

translations.literal: Earlier popular rumor held that Taizong was not male; Grand Imperial Consort Chen had originally been concubine to Li Dao-er, and street talk sometimes said Yu was Dao-er's son.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier popular rumor held that Taizong was impotent; Grand Imperial Consort Chen had originally been concubine to Li Dao'er, and street talk sometimes said Yu was Dao'er's son.

sentences.zh: 昱每出入去來，常自稱劉統，或自號李將軍。

translations.literal: Each time Yu went out or came in he often called himself Liu Tong, or styled himself General Li.
translations.idiomatic: Each time Yu went out or came in he often called himself Liu Tong or styled himself General Li.

sentences.zh: 與右衞翼輦營女子私通，每從之遊，持數千錢，供酒肉之費。

translations.literal: He had private relations with a woman of the Right Guard Sedan Escort camp; each time he went with her on outings carrying several thousand cash for wine and meat expenses.
translations.idiomatic: He had a secret affair with a woman of the Right Guard sedan escort camp; whenever he went out with her he carried several thousand cash for wine and meat.

sentences.zh: 阮佃夫腹心人張羊為佃夫所委信。

translations.literal: Ruan Tian-fu's trusted man Zhang Yang was entrusted and trusted by Tian-fu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Tianfu's trusted follower Zhang Yang was fully entrusted by Tianfu.

sentences.zh: 佃夫敗，叛走，後捕得，昱自於承明門以車轢殺之。

translations.literal: When Tian-fu fell, Yang rebelled and fled; later when captured, Yu personally had him crushed to death with a cart wheel at Chenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianfu fell, Yang rebelled and fled; later when captured, Yu personally had him crushed to death under cart wheels at Chenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 杜延載、沈勃、杜幼文、孫超，皆躬運矛鋋，手自臠割。

translations.literal: Du Yan-zai, Shen Bo, Du You-wen, and Sun Chao—all personally wielded spears and halberds and with their own hands performed dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Du Yanzai, Shen Bo, Du Youwen, and Sun Chao all personally wielded spears and halberds and with their own hands performed dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 執幼文兄叔文於玄武湖北，昱馳馬執矟，自往刺之。

translations.literal: Holding You-wen's elder brother Shu-wen north of Xuanwu Lake, Yu spurred his horse, grasped a spear, and personally went to stab him.
translations.idiomatic: They held Youwen's elder brother Shuwen north of Xuanwu Lake; Yu spurred his horse, grasped a spear, and personally rode to stab him.

sentences.zh: 制露車一乘，其上施篷，乘以出入，從者不過數十人。

translations.literal: He had made one open carriage with a canopy mounted on it, riding it to go in and out; followers numbered no more than several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: He had one open carriage built with a canopy on top and rode it to go in and out; followers numbered no more than several dozen.

sentences.zh: 羽儀追之恒不及；

translations.literal: Imperial escort pursuing him constantly could not catch up;
translations.idiomatic: The imperial escort that pursued him never caught up;

sentences.zh: 又各慮禍，亦不敢追尋，唯整部伍，別在一處瞻望而已。

translations.literal: Moreover each feared calamity and also dared not pursue; they could only keep ranks in order and stand apart in one place to watch.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover each feared calamity and dared not pursue; they could only keep ranks in order and stand apart watching.

sentences.zh: 凡諸鄙事，過目則能，鍛鍊金銀，裁衣作帽，莫不精絕。

translations.literal: Of all vulgar crafts, what passed his eyes he could do; forging and refining gold and silver, cutting clothes and making hats—none were not exquisitely perfect.
translations.idiomatic: In all vulgar crafts he was instantly capable—forging gold and silver, cutting clothes and making hats—none were not exquisitely perfect.

sentences.zh: 未嘗吹篪，執管便韻。

translations.literal: He had never blown the chi flute, yet grasping the pipe produced proper tones.
translations.idiomatic: He had never studied the chi flute, yet grasping the pipe produced proper tones.

sentences.zh: 天性好殺，以此為歡，一日無事，輒慘慘不樂。

translations.literal: He was by nature fond of killing and took this as pleasure; one day without business and he was wretchedly unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved killing and took it as his pleasure; one day without killing and he was miserably unhappy.

sentences.zh: 內外百司，人不自保，殿省憂遑，夕不及旦。

translations.literal: Inside and outside the hundred offices, men could not protect themselves; palace offices were anxious and alarmed, evening not reaching dawn.
translations.idiomatic: Throughout the hundred offices inside and outside, no one could protect himself; palace offices lived in dread from evening until dawn.

sentences.zh: 齊王順天人之心，潛圖廢立，與直閤將軍王敬則謀之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi, following the hearts of Heaven and men, secretly plotted deposition and installation and consulted with Direct Attendant-General Wang Jing-ze.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qi, following Heaven and the people's will, secretly plotted deposition and installation and consulted with Direct Attendant-General Wang Jingze.

sentences.zh: 七月七日，昱乘露車，從二百許人，無復鹵簿羽儀，往青園尼寺，晚至新安寺就曇度道人飲酒。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode the open carriage with about two hundred men, no longer with armed escort or feathered banners, going to Qingyuan Nunnery; in the evening he arrived at Xin'an Temple to drink with the Daoist Tan-du.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month Yu rode his open carriage with about two hundred men, without armed escort or feathered banners, going to Qingyuan Nunnery; in the evening he reached Xin'an Temple to drink with the Daoist priest Tan Du.

sentences.zh: 醉，夕扶還於仁壽殿東阿氈幄中臥。

translations.literal: Drunk, at evening he was supported back to lie in the felt tent at the eastern cove of the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk, at evening he was supported back to lie in the felt tent east of the Hall of Benevolent Longevity.

sentences.zh: 時昱出入無恒，省內諸閤，夜皆不閉。

translations.literal: At that time Yu's comings and goings had no fixed pattern; the various gates within the palace offices at night were all left unclosed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yu's comings and goings had no fixed pattern; within the palace offices all gates were left unclosed at night.

sentences.zh: 且羣下畏相逢值，無敢出者。

translations.literal: Moreover subordinates feared encountering him; none dared go out.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover subordinates feared encountering him and none dared go out.

sentences.zh: 宿衞並逃避，內外無相禁攝。

translations.literal: Night guards all fled; inside and outside there was no mutual restraint or control.
translations.idiomatic: Night guards all fled; inside and outside there was no one to enforce control.

sentences.zh: 王敬則先結昱左右楊玉夫、楊萬年、呂欣之、湯成之、陳奉伯、張石留、羅僧智、鍾千載、嚴道福、雷道賜、戴昭祖、許啟、戚元寶、盛道泰、鍾千秋、王天寶、公上延孫、俞成、錢道寶、馬敬之、陳寶直、吳璩之、劉印魯、唐天寶、俞孫等二十五人，謀共取昱。

translations.literal: Wang Jing-ze first won over Yu's attendants Yang Yu-fu, Yang Wan-nian, Lü Xin-zhi, Tang Cheng-zhi, Chen Feng-bo, Zhang Shi-liu, Luo Seng-zhi, Zhong Qian-zai, Yan Dao-fu, Lei Dao-ci, Dai Zhao-zu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuan-bao, Sheng Dao-tai, Zhong Qian-qiu, Wang Tian-bao, Gongshang Yan-sun, Yu Cheng, Qian Dao-bao, Ma Jing-zhi, Chen Bao-zhi, Wu Qu-zhi, Liu Yin-lu, Tang Tian-bao, Yu Sun, and twenty-five others in all, plotting together to seize Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingze first won over Yu's attendants Yang Yufu, Yang Wannian, Lü Xinzhi, Tang Chengzhi, Chen Fengbo, Zhang Shiliu, Luo Sengzhi, Zhong Qianzai, Yan Daofu, Lei Daoci, Dai Zhaozu, Xu Qi, Qi Yuanbao, Sheng Datai, Zhong Qianqiu, Wang Tianbao, Gongshang Yansun, Yu Cheng, Qian Daobao, Ma Jingzhi, Chen Baozhi, Wu Quzhi, Liu Yinlu, Tang Tianbao, Yu Sun, and twenty-five others in all, plotting together to seize Yu.

sentences.zh: 其夕，敬則出外，玉夫見昱醉熟無所知，乃與萬年同入氈幄內，以昱防身刀斬之。

translations.literal: That evening Jing-ze went outside; Yu-fu saw Yu drunk deep and without awareness, and together with Wan-nian entered the felt tent and beheaded him with Yu's personal dagger.
translations.idiomatic: That evening Jingze went outside; Yufu saw Yu drunk into oblivion and, together with Wannian, entered the felt tent and beheaded him with Yu's personal dagger.

sentences.zh: 奉伯提昱首，依常行法，稱敕開承明門出，以首與敬則，馳至領軍府，以首呈齊王。

translations.literal: Feng-bo carried Yu's head; following the usual procedure, proclaimed an edict and opened Chenming Gate to go out; he gave the head to Jing-ze and galloped to the army commander's residence, presenting the head to Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Fengbo carried Yu's head; following usual procedure, proclaimed an edict, opened Chenming Gate, gave the head to Jingze, and galloped to the army commander's residence to present it to Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 王乃戎服，率左右數十人，稱行還，開承明門入。

translations.literal: The Prince donned military dress, led several dozen attendants, claimed to be returning from an outing, and entered through Chenming Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The prince donned military dress, led several dozen attendants, claimed to be returning from an outing, and entered through Chenming Gate.

sentences.zh: 昱他夕每開門，門者震懾不敢視，至是弗之疑。

translations.literal: On other nights whenever Yu opened the gate, gatekeepers trembled in awe and dared not look; on this occasion they did not suspect.
translations.idiomatic: On other nights whenever Yu opened the gate, gatekeepers trembled in awe and dared not look up; this time they suspected nothing.

sentences.zh: 齊王既入，曉，乃奉太后令奉迎安成王。

translations.literal: Once Prince of Qi had entered, at dawn he then presented the empress dowager's order to welcome Prince of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Once Prince of Qi had entered, at dawn he presented the empress dowager's order to welcome Prince of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：喪國亡家之主，雖適末同途，發軫或異也。

translations.literal: The historian says: Lords who lose state and destroy family—though their ends follow the same road, their starting points may differ.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: rulers who lose their states and destroy their houses—though their ends follow the same road, their starting points may differ.

sentences.zh: 前廢帝卑遊褻幸，皆龍駕帝飾，傳警清路；

translations.literal: Emperor Fei I in lowly roaming and intimate favor still had dragon carriages and imperial adornment, transmitted alarms clearing the road;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Fei I in lowly roaming and dissolute outings still had dragon carriages and imperial trappings, with heralds clearing the road;

sentences.zh: 蒼梧王則藏璽懷紱，魚服忘反，危冠短服，匹馬孤征。

translations.literal: Prince of Cangwu by contrast hid the seal and clasped the ribbon, wore common garb forgetting return, perilous cap and short dress, a single horse on a lone journey.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Cangwu by contrast hid the seal and clasped the ribbon, wore commoner's garb and forgot to return, perilous cap and short dress, a single horse on a lone journey.

sentences.zh: 至於殞身覆祚，其理若一。

translations.literal: As for perishing in person and overturning the succession—the principle is as one.
translations.idiomatic: As for perishing in person and overturning the succession—the principle is the same.

sentences.zh: 姬、夏之隆，質文異尚，亡國之道，其亦然乎。

translations.literal: In the splendor of Zhou and Xia, substance and ornament differed in esteem—does the path to losing a state follow the same pattern?
translations.idiomatic: In the splendor of Zhou and Xia, substance and ornament were valued differently—does the path to ruin follow the same pattern?

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation notes
translations.idiomatic: Textual collation notes

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛卯 下有辛未。

translations.literal: "Winter, tenth month, xinmao"—below there is xinwei.
translations.idiomatic: Under "Winter, tenth month, xinmao" the text also has xinwei.

sentences.zh: 按是月庚戌朔，二十二日辛未，無辛卯。

translations.literal: According to this month, gengxu was the first day; the twenty-second day was xinwei—there was no xinmao.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on gengxu; the twenty-second day was xinwei—there was no xinmao.

sentences.zh: 以越州刺史陳伯紹為交州刺史 張森楷校勘記云：「按明帝紀，泰始五年，伯紹為交州刺史。

translations.literal: "Inspector of Yuezhou Chen Bo-zhao was made Inspector of Jiaozhou"—Zhang Sen-kai's collation notes state: "According to Emperor Ming's annals, in the fifth year of Taishi, Bo-zhao was Inspector of Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: "Inspector of Yuezhou Chen Bozhao was made inspector of Jiaozhou"—Zhang Senkai's collation notes state: "According to Emperor Ming's annals, in the fifth year of Taishi Bozhao was inspector of Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，置越州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Yuezhou was established.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhou was established in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 南齊書州郡志云，元徽二年，陳伯紹為越州刺史，當即指此。

translations.literal: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies in the Book of Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui Chen Bo-zhao was Inspector of Yuezhou—this must refer to the present passage.
translations.idiomatic: The Monograph on Provinces and Commanderies in the Book of Southern Qi says that in the second year of Yuanhui Chen Bozhao was inspector of Yuezhou—this must refer to the present passage.

sentences.zh: 此當是以交州刺史陳伯紹為越州刺史，刻譌互倒。」

translations.literal: This should read that Inspector of Jiaozhou Chen Bo-zhao was made Inspector of Yuezhou—a carving error transposing the two."
translations.idiomatic: This should read that inspector of Jiaozhou Chen Bozhao was made inspector of Yuezhou—a carving error transposed the two."

sentences.zh: 五月壬午「壬午」各本並作「壬子」，據南史、建康實錄、通鑑改。

translations.literal: "Fifth month, renwu"—"renwu" in all editions alike reads "renzi"; changed according to the History of Southern Dynasties, Veritable Records of Jiankang, and Comprehensive Mirror.
translations.idiomatic: "Fifth month, renwu"—every edition reads renzi for renwu; emended per the History of Southern Dynasties, Veritable Records of Jiankang, and Comprehensive Mirror.

sentences.zh: 按是月辛未朔，十三日壬午，無壬子。

translations.literal: According to this month, xinwei was the first day; the thirteenth day was renwu—there was no renzi.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on xinwei; the thirteenth day was renwu—there was no renzi.

sentences.zh: 賊黨杜黑蠡丁文豪分軍向朱雀航「杜黑蠡」魏書作「杜黑騾」。

translations.literal: "Rebel partisans Du Hei-li and Ding Wen-hao divided forces toward Zhuque floating bridge"—in the Wei Shu "Du Hei-li" is written as "Du Hei-lü."
translations.idiomatic: "Rebel partisans Du Heili and Ding Wenhao divided forces toward the Zhuque floating bridge"—the Wei Shu reads Du Heili as Du Heilü.

sentences.zh: 甲午 各本並作「戊午」，據局本及南史、建康實錄改。

translations.literal: "On jiawu day"—all editions alike read "wuwu"; changed according to the Bureau edition, History of Southern Dynasties, and Veritable Records of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: "On jiawu day"—every edition reads wuwu; emended per the Bureau edition, History of Southern Dynasties, and Veritable Records of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 是月辛未朔，二十四日甲午，無戊午。

translations.literal: That month xinwei was the first day; the twenty-fourth day was jiawu—there was no wuwu.
translations.idiomatic: That month began on xinwei; the twenty-fourth day was jiawu—there was no wuwu.

sentences.zh: 撫軍典籤茅恬開東府納賊「撫軍」南史作「車騎」，建康實錄作「護軍」。

translations.literal: "Registry Clerk of the Army Who Tranquilizes the Army Mao Tian opened the Eastern Office to admit rebels"—"Army Who Tranquilizes the Army" in the History of Southern Dynasties is written as "General of Chariots and Cavalry," and in the Veritable Records of Jiankang as "General of the Guard."
translations.idiomatic: "Registry clerk of the Army Who Tranquilizes the Army Mao Tian opened the Eastern Office to admit rebels"—the History of Southern Dynasties reads "Army Who Tranquilizes the Army" as "General of Chariots and Cavalry," and the Veritable Records of Jiankang as "General of the Guard."

sentences.zh: 鎮北將軍南徐州刺史建平王景素進號征北將軍 各本並脫「南」字，據景素傳補。

translations.literal: "General Who Tranquilizes the North and Inspector of South Xuzhou Prince of Jianping Jing-su was advanced in rank to General Who Campaigns North"—all editions alike omit the character "South"; restored according to Jing-su's biography.
translations.idiomatic: "General Who Tranquilizes the North and inspector of South Xuzhou Prince of Jianping Jingsu was promoted to general who campaigns north"—every edition omits "South"; restored per Jingsu's biography.

sentences.zh: 穀人五斛 各本並脫「人」字，據元龜二０七補。

translations.literal: "Five hu of grain per person"—all editions alike omit the character "person"; restored according to Yuan Gui 207.
translations.idiomatic: "Five hu of grain per person"—every edition omits "person"; restored per Yuan Gui 207.

sentences.zh: 八月庚子 按是月癸亥朔，無庚子，初三日庚午，庚子或是庚午之譌。

translations.literal: "Eighth month, gengzi"—according to this month, guihai was the first day—there was no gengzi; the third day was gengwu; gengzi may be a corruption of gengwu.
translations.idiomatic: "Eighth month, gengzi"—that month began on guihai, so there was no gengzi; the third day was gengwu; gengzi is likely a corruption of gengwu.

sentences.zh: 而國度弘費「弘」各本並作「引」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: "Yet state expenditures are vast"—"vast" in all editions alike is written as "extend"; changed according to Yuan Gui 471.
translations.idiomatic: "Yet state expenditures are vast"—every edition reads "extend" for "vast"; emended per Yuan Gui 471.

sentences.zh: 則氓隸齊歡「隸」各本並作「祇」，據元龜四七一改。

translations.literal: "Then commoners and slaves alike rejoice"—"slaves" in all editions alike is written as "only"; changed according to Yuan Gui 471.
translations.idiomatic: "Then commoners and slaves alike rejoice"—every edition reads "only" for "slaves"; emended per Yuan Gui 471.

sentences.zh: 驍騎將軍全景文為南豫州刺史「驍騎」各本並作「驃騎」，據南齊書呂安國傳全景文附傳改。

translations.literal: "General of Valiant Cavalry Quan Jing-wen was made Inspector of South Yuzhou"—"Valiant Cavalry" in all editions alike is written as "Rapid Cavalry"; changed according to the attached biography of Quan Jing-wen in Lü An-guo's biography in the Book of Southern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: "General of valiant cavalry Quan Jingwen was appointed inspector of South Yuzhou"—every edition reads "rapid cavalry" for "valiant cavalry"; emended per Quan Jingwen's attached biography in Lü Anguo's biography in the Book of Southern Qi.
